title: Detailed balance in large language model-driven agents
abstract: arXiv:2512.10047v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Large language model (LLM)-driven agents are emerging as a powerful new paradigm for solving complex problems. Despite the empirical success of these practices, a theoretical framework to understand and unify their macroscopic dynamics remains lacking. This paper proposes a method based on the least action principle to estimate the underlying generative directionality of LLMs embedded within agents. By experimentally measuring the transition probabilities between LLM-generated states, we report evidence consistent with a tendency toward detailed balance in LLM-generated transitions, indicating that LLM generation may not be achieved by generally learning rule sets and strategies, but rather by implicitly learning a class of underlying potential functions that may transcend different LLM architectures and prompt templates. translated_title: 大语言模型驱动的智能体中的细致平衡
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）驱动的智能体正在成为解决复杂问题的强大新范式。尽管这些实践在经验上取得了成功，但目前仍缺乏一个能够理解和统一其宏观动力学的理论框架。本文提出了一种基于最小作用量原理的方法，用于估计嵌入智能体中的大语言模型的潜在生成方向性。通过实验测量大语言模型生成状态之间的转移概率，我们报告了与大语言模型生成转移中呈现细致平衡倾向相一致的证据，这表明大语言模型的生成可能不是通过一般性地学习规则集和策略来实现的，而是通过隐式学习一类可能超越不同大语言模型架构和提示模板的潜在势函数来实现的。据我们所知，这为大语言模型生成动力学提供了一种有效的宏观描述。
tldr: 本文基于最小作用量原理，通过测量大语言模型智能体状态间的转移概率，发现其生成过程呈现细致平衡的倾向，表明LLM生成可能源于隐式学习的一类超越不同架构和提示模板的潜在势函数。
en_tdlr: By measuring transition probabilities between LLM-generated states based on the least action principle, this paper reveals a tendency toward detailed balance in LLM-driven agents, suggesting that LLM generation may arise from implicitly learned potential functions that transcend different architectures and prompt templates.
